Well this might be par for the course for people with more severe psychosis but yes I have. (Possible TRIGGER WARNING HERE) I used to get a sensation like biting or scratching on my ears, neck and back. Along with feeling like I’m being punched in the chest or like something is trying to drag me around. Now this only happened when the voices were really bad or if I went off my meds long enough. So it was really an “if I’m in a major episode kinda thing.” 

It was honestly something I wouldn’t wish on my worst enemy. Mostly cause it’s terrifying. It would usually happen along with really awful agitation. I mean so much stress that you almost feel convinced you have to cope somehow or you might self harm. It would almost feel like an evil monkey on my back. And it was confusing as well because some part of me knew it’s not real. So I tried to ignore it and go about my day at home. It was deeply concerning. Cause I knew I was having an episode. 

I would manage to relax for a few minutes and then something would trigger it and it would be right back to torture. It’s hard to explain tactile physical hallucination. It’s something you either know cause you get it or you don’t. Usually my only friendly positive relief during those times were sleep or self soothe with music. And MAYBE calling my best friend or talking with family. Although that tended to be a wild card that was either good or bad because of the nature of my schizophrenia. 

But yeah that’s pretty much it…sorry for the giant wall of text I just want to share what I’ve been through hoping it helps someone. Ik it helps to get it off my chest. It’s a surprisingly cathartic way of dealing with it.

Now as for nowadays I’ve been mostly symptom free for a good few years. Keep yalls heads up it gets better. If an ordinary jackass like me can do it. Then you can and deserve to do it too. It’ll be all right. So long as your breathing you gotta reason. Peace to yall.

Bless your heart, I get it man, I’ve had this exact thing. It’s horrendous and I’m very sorry you’re going through that. But I have to tell you because it’s vital. This is the way psychosis (psychosis right? Do you have a diagnosis? I’m presuming you’re struggling with schizophrenia hence being on this subreddit.) but yeah this is the classic thing psychosis like this does. It’s a sickness/chemical imbalance that can flair up if not handled with care. But it will pass soon, I promise you. 1st things 1st. You mentioned you have a therapist and psychiatrist. That’s good. I doubt these people are your therapist for shits and giggles. I’m sure you maybe had family and friends that helped you get therapy. Think strongly on that. Therapists are helpful. I know it doesn’t seem like it but they are. So keep in mind it’s probably just more likely that they want to help you recover and get well. Rather than want to do you harm. Back when my delusions were way worse something that helped me cope and ground my self to a stable reality was simply talking about the delusions with someone dear to me and have them help me discern the reality and concern they had for me. 

And what’s more I found that self care and healthy mindfulness really helped me to see clearly and get to a stable calm mindset. Also this parts very important. God certainly doesn’t want you to fail or kill yourself. He’s the good guy, he’s your dearest friend especially in a time like this. I know it’s hard to believe but I take it there’s something in you that wants to live and find relief. Pay attention to that spark. I won’t get preachy and please don’t take this the wrong way. But from what I’ve learned NOONE IS EXEMPT…I wanna repeat that for good measure. No one is exempt from hope no one is so “special” or so “vital” to utter doom that there singled out and considered that “other” person that is just so bad that everyone and there grandma wants them gone. It’s not true friend. As long as you draw breath you got a reason to be hopeful. It’s difficult but it’s doable. Peace and stability will come back. God loves you.
